safety_lead_time.comparison_action: Increase from SAP 0.0 days to recommended 3.07 days

narrative: Material PL3__MDD5C33C shows erratic, right-skewed daily demand averaging 681 units with a CV of 0.623, indicating significant day-to-day variability with frequent zero-demand days. Lead times are moderately variable at 3.48 days mean (CV 0.419), with transport being the dominant source of uncertainty at 60% of variance. The current SAP policy of zero safety stock exposes the operation to frequent stockouts; the recommended (r,Q) continuous-review policy with safety stock 2,091 and order quantity 14,526 achieves the 95% service-level target while reducing total annual costs by 57.8%. The storage capacity constraint of 16,617 units is exactly met, leaving no surplus buffer beyond the embedded safety stock.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Erratic demand with moderate lead-time variability warrants continuous monitoring and a fixed-quantity reorder policy. Periodic review would add unnecessary exposure during the review interval given the demand volatility.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage cap binds exactly at 16,617 units (safety_stock 2,091 + order_quantity 14,526). Any upward revision to safety stock would require a proportional reduction in order quantity, increasing ordering frequency and cost. Additional storage capacity would unlock a better cost-service trade-off.
